newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes slide lower for outrights, grades even.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes slide lower for outrights, grades even.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slid lower for outright benchmark prices, but domestic grade barrels failed to establish momentum in a low volume Thursday session, traders said.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing lost 30 cents to talk late at $19.85-95 a barrel, and July WTI edged around 5 cts higher than front month.

Late selling in NYMEX futures depressed cash WTI. Paper markets were pushed lower by profit-taking and technical selling. News in the market was limited to the U.N. maintaining broad sanctions on Iraq at a regular 60-day review.
Confirmed deals saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sell at 7 cts and 8 cts under WTI/Cushing, steady from Wednesday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was done at a 50 cts discount late in the session, again even with yesterday dealings.
Traders pegged Midland/WTI at the last trade, 31 cts under the WTI/Cushing value, at the weaker end of talked ranges.
West Texas Sour/Midland lost some ground, moving at WTI/Cushing -$1.75, 5 cts weaker than late Wednesday.
Eugene Island sour barrels moved in small volumes at WTI/Cushing -$1.55, steady from Wednesday.
Sour crudes came under pressure from Iraqi Basrah Light offerings in the U.S. Gulf.
Overall, traders said industry functions kept many players out of the market.
"It was really dead in there, and we probably won't get any better until next week," said a cash broker in Texas.
